answers.M6-S1: When we badly want something, like being taller, we can be easily tricked into believing promises that are too good to be true.
answers.M6-S2: So the narrator won't ask anyone else, who would tell him the seed is fake. Secrecy hides Billy's trick and gives him an excuse if it fails.
answers.M6-S3: The narrator thinks Billy is doing him a special, generous favor. The reader can tell Billy is probably tricking him to get ten cents for worthless seed.
answers.M6-S4: He is secretly worried he won't grow and will be short like Uncle Alec, so he badly wants to be taller and jumps at any help.
answers.M6-S5: To make the seed sound magical and rare, and to explain why the narrator can't go get more himself or check Billy's story.
answers.M6-S6: It shows the seed isn't working, but the narrator still hopes and makes excuses, which hints he has been fooled and adds humor.
answers.M6-S7: It explains why the narrator believes Billy: Billy's height seems like proof the seed works, making his story convincing to the narrator.
answers.M6-S8: That people didn't really trust or care for Billy much, hinting he has a reputation for being sly or dishonest, so the offer is suspicious.
answers.M6-S9: He cares about his uncle and isn't insulting him, but he still doesn't want to be short like him; he wants to grow taller.
